text:
Anya Patel: Heads up — our eu-west canary (driver+fw+kernel bundle) is showing a modest Xid spike since the 14:00 rollout. Not yet service-impacting but visible in the canary cohort. https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/canary-eu-west
Devin Chen: saw that too, digging in. Which canary batch? sample size?
Anya Patel: deploy id cny-20251112-14-00, sample 30 nodes (mixed A100/RTX). infra-bot posted the rollout: 
infra-bot: Canary started: cny-20251112-14-00 · pools: gpu-eu-west-canary · image: driver-525.85/fw-1.2.3/kernel-6.4.8 · sample=30
Samir Khan: can you paste the quick logs? NVML/Xid lines are the priority. Also capture dmesg + nv_peer_mem?
Anya Patel: pasted snippets below:
```
[2025-11-12T14:05:31Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 62, pid=1245, GPU 0000:af:00:00: GPU SM reported a exception
[2025-11-12T14:05:31Z] nvidia: ecc_correctable: 12 ecc_uncorrectable: 0
[2025-11-12T14:05:33Z] container: warn: saw 3 consecutive Xid 62 on node gpu-canary-17
```
Devin Chen: okay repeated 62s on the same host. Run this quick collector on gpu-canary-17 and attach output:
```
infractl exec gpu-canary-17 -- bash -lc "dmesg | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.canary && nvidia-smi --query-gpu=ecc.errors.uncorrected,ecc.errors.corrected --format=csv -f /tmp/nvmm.canary"
```
Samir Khan: if we have ECC correctable creeping up it could be flaky DIMM or thermal. Ask oncall to check chassis logs and power cycling history. Also capture nv-hostengine and pld traces.
Maria Lopez: note on rollout policy — our canary gating checks only look at p99 latency + OOMs; we need an Xid counter alarm on canary cohort threshold to auto-hold. Filing a quick follow-up ticket.
Anya Patel: infractl outputs: attached gist but key bits: ecc.corrected increased to 19 on gpu0, dmesg shows repeated SM errors, and i2c sensor read spikes during the window.
Samir Khan: sounds like either driver/kernel interaction or a flaky card getting aggravated by new FW. Two parallel actions: 1) isolate affected nodes and run driver-only downgrade test; 2) run firmware-only subset to see if Xid persists.
Devin Chen: rolling a targeted rollback for the 6 nodes with >5 Xid events now. Command:
```
infractl rollback --nodes gpu-canary-17,gpu-canary-09,gpu-canary-21 --image=driver-525.84/fw-1.2.2
```
Anya Patel: thanks. Also capturing per-token cost/latency impact: no visible latency regression so far, just error counter.
infra-bot: Rollback initiated: rbk-20251112-14-12 by Devin Chen · nodes targeted: 3
Maria Lopez: after rollback, let's keep those nodes in a fenced pool and run a 24h burn-in with ECC stress tests and continuous nvml logging. If they repro, schedule hardware replace via spares.
Samir Khan: agree. Also we should add a short kernel module symbol map collector when Xid occurs — to get better stacks. I'll post a small script.
Devin Chen: quick ask — can eng-sre temporarily relax auto-drain for canary nodes? We don't want aggressive drains to mask the signal. Maria, want me to request that?
Maria Lopez: yes please request a hold for 1h while we triage, then re-enable. I'll update the rollout checklist to include Xid threshold and auto-hold.
Anya Patel: TL;DR: observed Xid62 spike on eu-west canary after driver+fw+kernel bundle. Rolling targeted rollback, isolating hosts for burn-in, adding Xid alarms to canary gating, and adding kernel-symbol capture on next run. Will post post-mortem if we confirm hardware vs software. :thumbsup:
Samir Khan: leaving a reminder — correlate with PCIe error counters and ambient temp trends, those often correlate with ECC bursts.
Devin Chen: logging collection uploaded to https://console.redwood.ai/logs/canary/cny-20251112-14-00, will follow up when rollback completes.
infra-bot: Rollback completed: rbk-20251112-14-18 · 3 nodes · status=success
Anya Patel: rollback succeeded, spike subsided on those nodes. continuing burn-in and will run fw-only canary tomorrow at 09:00 UTC with stricter Xid gating. Thanks team.
